draft.title: Collecting data
card: Data is the information a group collects to answer its research question. A valid method measures what the question is asking about.
Survey
a set of questions that people answer. It suits things people can report, such as how many hours they sleep.
Fitness test
a standard task that gives a number, such as a 20 m sprint time. It suits questions about physical performance.
Observation
watching and noting what people do, such as how often players pass a ball. Record results carefully: use the same method each time and write each result down straight away.
draft.remember: Pick the method that measures what the question asks, then record every result carefully.

a.q: A group asks whether a warm-up changes 20 m sprint times. Which method is the most valid way to collect data?
opts: Time each student's 20 m sprint with and without a warm-up
Ask students if they think a warm-up makes them faster
Watch students warm up and note how long they stretch
Survey students on how often they play sport each week
a.why: The question is about sprint times, so timing the sprints measures exactly that. Asking what students think is tempting, but it records opinions and not their actual times.
a.clue: Which method gives you the sprint times themselves?

b.q: Ravi's group wants to know how often Year 11 students pass the ball in netball games. A member suggests recording the results later from memory. What is the best advice?
opts: Observe games and tally each pass as it happens
Survey players on how often they think they pass
Time each player over a 20 m sprint
Observe games and write up the tallies the next day
b.why: Passing is behaviour that can be watched, so observation suits it. Tallying as it happens keeps the record accurate. Writing it up the next day uses the right method but risks forgotten or wrong results.
b.clue: Choose the method that fits behaviour, and record it at once.

a.best: Time each student's 20 m sprint with and without a warm-up

b.best: Observe games and tally each pass as it happens

problems.detail: The clue 'Choose the method that fits behaviour, and record it at once' names both parts of the right answer (observation and recording straight away). A student can match it to the option without understanding why observation suits behaviour.
